learning_outcomes.text: Student learns the basic concepts of root locus (RL) and its interpretation
Student gains the basic principles of feedback sensors, constructs models and integrates them with the control system block diagram.
Student observes the behavior of the control system designed by the use of a computer program.
Student learns the basic principles of Bode diagram technique and has knowledge of integrating into a control system.
Students gains the knowledge of designing P, PD, PD ve PID controllers.

syllabus_topics: Course Policy. Introduction. Basic concepts in the design of control systems
The use of time domain and frequency domain techniques in the control system design.
Basic definitions used for root locus. Rules of drawing root locus for a given open loop pole/zero configuration of an open loop transfer function
Root locus with respect to any parameter. Root contours. Root locus of systems with transportation lag.
Fundamental concepts in the design of feedforward controllers (compensators, filters) by using root locus technique.
P, PI and PID-controller design. Analytical design of P, PI, PD and PID controllers. Lag and lead compensators as controllers.
Basic definition and characteristics of frequency response.
Bode plots; constant gain, integral/derivative factors, first order factors, second order factors, resonance.
Polar plots. Closed loop frequency response from the polar plot of open loop frequency response.
Relative stability. Phase and gain crossover frequencies. Phase margin. Gain margin.
Constant N circles. Log-magnitude versus phase plots. Nichols diagram.
Analytical design methods for lag, lead and PID controllers. PD controllers.
